title: Authority of Scripture
definition: The authority of Scripture is the truth that the Bible is God's Word and therefore serves as the final and supreme authority for faith, doctrine, and daily living.
summary: Because Scripture is God's Word, it has the right to govern what believers believe and how they live.
christFocus: Jesus consistently affirmed the authority of Scripture, submitted to it, taught from it, fulfilled it, and used it as the foundation of truth throughout His earthly ministry.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The authority of Scripture rests upon its divine origin. Because God is the ultimate author of Scripture, the Bible carries His authority and speaks truthfully to every area of life. Scripture is not merely a collection of religious writings or human opinions. It is God's revealed Word given to guide, correct, teach, encourage, and equip His people.

This means Scripture stands above personal preference, cultural pressure, church tradition, spiritual experience, and human reasoning. The believer does not come to Scripture as judge over it, but as a servant under it.

The authority of Scripture is also gracious. God has not left His people to guess what is true. He has spoken clearly enough to call sinners to Christ, teach His people how to live, expose sin, comfort the suffering, and guide the church in faithful doctrine and mission.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people struggle to know what is true because they are surrounded by conflicting opinions, philosophies, emotions, and cultural messages. Understanding the authority of Scripture gives believers a trustworthy foundation that does not shift with changing circumstances.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Evaluate your beliefs, decisions, relationships, ministry methods, and priorities through the lens of Scripture. When God's Word challenges your assumptions, choose submission over self-reliance and ask, 'What does Scripture say?'
